subject: Independent verification of the architect implemented instrumentation scope correction

recomputed.note: Restored byte identical after a deviation of my own, see protocolDeviation.

protocolDeviation.statement: I changed and committed the inspection object before I had read directive 0030.
detail: Directive 0030 was placed in the inbox at 16:16. I did not read the inbox before my next edit block, which is a breach of the cyclic reading duty of my assignment.

Two changes of mine touched the object. The first moved IMetricsBus to namespace scope, which made the multi bus case runnable at all; the hash bound by directive 0030 already contains that change, so it is part of the inspection object and not a deviation.
The second added a helper that reports a missing measurement by name instead of a bare cancelled task. That change left the bound state and has been reverted byte identical.
protocolDeviation.correction: commit caf6fb9b restores the bound bytes; all five hashes recomputed above match.
protocolDeviation.proposalInsteadOfChange: The barrier message helper is offered as a proposal. Without it the isolation case fails as a cancelled task after thirty seconds at the await of the second provider measurement, which names the line but not the assurance.

contractVerification.point: Provider isolation for consume and for send
contractVerification.method: Static: the send instrument resolves its state from transportContext.LogContext at LogContextInstrumentationExtensions.cs:323, so it does not depend on an ambient asynchronous caller context; every other instrument resolves from its own log context. Dynamic: the isolation case collects consume and send measurements of both providers separately and asserts the collectors of the other provider are empty.

contractVerification.point: Shared state of several buses of one provider
contractVerification.method: One state per IMeterFactory, created through a Lazy with ExecutionAndPublication and stored in a ConditionalWeakTable keyed by that factory. The multi bus case publishes from both buses and observes two send measurements through the single meter factory of the provider.

contractVerification.point: Provider lifetime through IMeterFactory and behaviour after dispose
contractVerification.method: The isolation case disposes the first provider and then proves that the second still records. No manual meter dispose path exists in either file, so the meter lifetime stays with the factory that created it.

contractVerification.point: Unchanged public meter, instrument, tag, unit and description contracts
contractVerification.method: Mechanical comparison of all instrument declarations before and after the correction: 32 before, 32 after, identical in option key, instrument kind, generic type, unit and description.

contractVerification.point: No public API or binary contract change
contractVerification.method: Public member census of the three changed product files: 14 before and after in LogContextInstrumentationExtensions, 22 before and after in LogContext, 27 before and after in BaseHostConfiguration. The new type is internal and ViciOne.ServiceBus grants InternalsVisibleTo to nothing.

contractVerification.point: The non dependency injection fallback stays functional and cannot take over a dependency injection provider
contractVerification.method: TryConfigure(InstrumentationOptions) creates the fallback once under a double checked lock and is the only writer. It never binds a log context of a provider and never blocks the provider path.
contractVerification.observation: The fallback is nevertheless the resolution of last resort for any log context that carries no binding. In a process that mixes both paths, a dependency injection context that is not reached by one of the copy paths would record into the fallback meter. In the current test corpus this cannot occur, because no test calls UseInstrumentation and the fallback therefore stays null; an unbound context then records nothing.

contractVerification.method: The state per meter factory is created through Lazy with ExecutionAndPublication, so a concurrent race creates it once. Binding takes a lock around remove and add. Reading uses the thread safe lookup of the table and a volatile read of the fallback. The fallback creation is a double checked lock with volatile write.

contractVerification.point: No permanent strong reference to a root provider or a meter factory
contractVerification.method: Both tables are ConditionalWeakTable, whose entries use ephemeron semantics, so a value that references its own key does not keep that key alive. This matters here: the default meter factory sets the scope of a created meter to itself, so the stored state does reference its key. With ephemeron semantics the entry is still collectable. Neither table references an IServiceProvider.

executedCommands.note: The three warnings are pre existing package source and nullable warnings, none from this block.
Run against the restored, hash identical inspection object.

mutationProbe.mutation: Every provider is bound to the first instrumentation state that was created, which is the removed first provider wins behaviour.
mutationProbe.message: No consume measurement of the second provider was observed through the meter factory of that provider
mutationProbe.revert: The product file was restored through git checkout; its hash matches the bound value above, and the combined run was green again.
mutationProbe.honestLimitation: Repeating this probe against the restored test file would surface the same failure at the same await as a cancelled task after thirty seconds, because the bound version carries no message helper.

verdict: The correction satisfies every point of the product contract of ANSWER 0029 that can be verified statically and by the focused run. No defect found; no QUESTION raised. Three residual observations are reported for the architect in INSTRUMENTATION_SCOPE_PROOF.json and are not defects of the current corpus.
